title: MoonPhasesClear
question: Why does the Moon change shape?
hook: The Moon never changes shape. The Sun always lights exactly half of it, and what changes is how much of that half faces you. Turn the Moon round its orbit, watch it rise from any latitude, and see why a crescent smiles near the equator.

explainer.title: Always half lit
explainer.text: The Moon makes no light. Sunlight always lights one half of it, like any ball in sunshine. The phases are how much of that lit half is turned towards Earth: none at new moon, half at the quarters, all of it at full moon.

explainer.title: Eight names, one cycle
explainer.text: From new moon the lit part grows (waxing) through crescent, first quarter and gibbous to full, then shrinks (waning) through gibbous, last quarter and crescent. The share of the disc lit is (1 − cos e) ÷ 2, where e is the Sun–Moon angle in our sky.

explainer.title: Two kinds of month
explainer.text: The Moon goes once round Earth against the stars in about 27.3 days. But Earth moves round the Sun meanwhile, so the phases repeat only every 29.5 days on average.

explainer.title: Each phase keeps its hours
explainer.text: The Moon rises on average about 50 minutes later each day. A full moon rises at sunset, a first quarter is high at sunset, and a last quarter hangs in the morning sky. Near the equator an evening crescent lies on its back, and south of the equator the Moon looks turned round.

explainer.title: The same face
explainer.text: The Moon spins once per orbit, so the same side always faces us. A slow wobble called libration lets us see about 59% of its surface over time. The faint glow on a crescent's dark part is earthshine, sunlight bounced off Earth.

explainer.title: Not Earth's shadow
explainer.text: The phases are not Earth's shadow, which reaches the Moon only in a lunar eclipse. Supermoons are full moons near the closest point of the orbit. Twelve lunar months make about 354 days, which is why the Islamic calendar moves through the seasons and lunisolar calendars add leap months.
